title: U.S. House · Louisiana's 6th District
area: Baton Rouge and parts of south-central Louisiana.

context.text: Louisiana's 2026 U.S. House elections use a "majority vote" (all-party) system: every candidate, regardless of party, appears on one ballot on November 3, 2026. If no candidate wins a majority, the top two finishers advance to a December 12, 2026 general election. The partisan primary and runoff originally scheduled for May and June 2026 were canceled after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in Louisiana v. Callais that the state's congressional map was an unconstitutional racial gerrymander, requiring a new map. This is an open seat: incumbent Cleo Fields (D), first elected in 2024, is not on the November 3 ballot.

candidates.name: Blake Miguez
candidates.currentRole: Louisiana State Senator, District 22 (since 2024); former Louisiana State Representative, District 49 (2015–2024)

summary.text: Blake Miguez is a Republican state senator from the New Iberia area, an oil and gas executive and attorney who served in the Louisiana House for nearly a decade before winning a Senate seat in 2023. He first ran for the U.S. Senate, then qualified for the 5th District, and entered the 6th District race on the final day of qualifying in August 2026. His residence, which he says is primarily in New Iberia, has been a point of contention in the race.

background.text: Born November 21, 1981, in Lafayette, Louisiana, and graduated from Catholic High School in New Iberia in 1999.
Earned a political science degree from Louisiana State University (2004) and a law degree from the Southern University Law Center (2008).
Works as an executive in the oil and gas industry and is a corporate attorney licensed in Louisiana, according to Wikipedia.
Won a February 2015 special election to the Louisiana House of Representatives, District 49, and served until January 2024.
Served as Majority Leader of the Louisiana House from January 2020 to January 2024.
Elected to the Louisiana Senate, District 22, in October 2023 and took office on January 8, 2024; is a member of the Louisiana Freedom Caucus.

Announced a campaign for the U.S. Senate against Sen. Bill Cassidy in June 2025 but did not appear on the May 16, 2026 primary ballot; he then ran for the 5th Congressional District, receiving a Trump endorsement in February 2026.

After the congressional primaries were canceled and districts redrawn, qualified for the 6th District on August 7, 2026; he says he has lived in both Baton Rouge and New Iberia and acknowledges his primary residence is in New Iberia, while Rick Edmonds disputes that he lives in the district.
Is a competitive shooter, a grand master of the U.S. Practical Shooting Association, and appeared on the History Channel's show Top Shot, according to Wikipedia.

positions.summary: Voted yes on SB 184, banning abortion once a fetal heartbeat is detectable, and on SB 342, increasing criminal penalties for abortion providers with no exception for rape or incest.
Voted yes on HB 596, which allowed adults 21 and older to carry a concealed handgun without a permit.
His campaign issues page calls for finishing the border wall, funding agents, ending catch-and-release and mandating E-Verify.
positions.quote: In Congress he’ll finish the wall, fund the agents, end catch-and-release, mandate E-Verify

positions.summary: His campaign issues page says he helped lead the effort to bar transgender athletes from girls' and women's sports and will carry that fight to Washington.
positions.quote: Blake helped lead the effort to keep men out of girls’ bathrooms and out of women’s sports.

positions.summary: His campaign issues page lists proof of citizenship among his election priorities and calls on Congress to pass the SAVE America Act.
positions.quote: Congress needs to pass the SAVE America Act and get it to the President’s desk.

record.text: Served in the Louisiana House of Representatives for District 49 (2015–2024); now serves in the Louisiana State Senate for District 22 (since 2024).
Voted yes on SB 184 (prohibiting abortion once a fetal heartbeat is detectable), which passed the Louisiana House 79-23 on May 29, 2019.
Voted yes on HB 596 (allowing adults 21 and older to carry a concealed handgun without a permit), which passed the Louisiana House 73-28 on May 5, 2021.

Voted yes on SB 342 (increasing criminal penalties for performing an abortion and expanding Louisiana's abortion ban, with no exception for rape or incest), which passed the Louisiana House 72-25 on June 2, 2022.

candidates.name: Rick Edmonds
candidates.currentRole: Louisiana State Senator, District 6 (since 2024); former Louisiana State Representative, District 66 (2016–2024)

summary.text: Rick Edmonds is a Republican state senator from Baton Rouge and a Baptist pastor who served in the Louisiana House from 2016 to 2024. He has run for statewide office before and chairs the Senate Education Committee. He originally entered the 5th District race and qualified for the 6th District in August 2026 after the maps were redrawn.

background.text: Born September 12, 1956, in Shreveport, Louisiana; lives in Baton Rouge.
Earned a B.A. from East Texas Baptist College (1979) and a Master of Divinity from New Orleans Baptist Theological Seminary (1990).

Worked as a pastor, including at Calvary Baptist Church in Shreveport; is currently senior pastor of First Baptist Church of McComb, Mississippi, which he says he commutes to while living in the 6th District.
Was previously involved with the Louisiana Family Forum, according to Wikipedia.
Won Louisiana House District 66 in 2015, defeating Republican incumbent Darrell Ourso, and served from January 2016 to January 2024.
Finished fourth with 11% of the vote in the 2018 special election for Louisiana Secretary of State.
Won Louisiana Senate District 6 in 2023, defeating Rep. Barry Ivey with 62% of the vote, and took office on January 8, 2024.
Chairs the Senate Education Committee in 2025-2026 and also serves on the Insurance, Judiciary A and Finance committees.
Originally announced for the 5th Congressional District; after the May elections were canceled and the maps redrawn, qualified for the 6th District in August 2026.

positions.summary: Said he would not favor restoring the expired enhanced Affordable Care Act subsidies, favors expanded health savings accounts, and supports the new Medicaid work requirements.
positions.quote: I am a strong proponent of the open market,

record.text: Served in the Louisiana House of Representatives for District 66 (2016–2024); now serves in the Louisiana State Senate for District 6 (since 2024).

candidates.name: Monique Appeaning

summary.text: Monique Appeaning is a Republican candidate who previously ran in the October 2023 primary for Louisiana House District 66 and did not advance to the runoff. No biographical statement beyond her candidacy history was found.

background.text: Ran in the 2023 nonpartisan primary for Louisiana House of Representatives District 66, which Emily Chenevert and Richie Edmonds advanced from.
Qualified as a Republican candidate for the 6th Congressional District in 2026.

priorities.text: Says she is running to lower costs, make communities safer, add jobs and increase accountability in Washington.
priorities.quote: lower costs, safer communities, more jobs, and real accountability in Washington

priorities.text: Lists tax relief proposals: no tax on tips, overtime or Social Security.
priorities.quote: No tax on tips, overtime, or Social Security

priorities.text: Lists strengthening and modernizing the military and rebuilding American manufacturing.

statements.quote: Build more homes to lower prices
statements.context: On her campaign home page, under "Affordable Living"

candidates.researchNotes: From her campaign site (appeaningforcongress.com); the site's issues section is a short list of slogans, and a Talk 107.3 report paraphrases her platform without direct quotes. No questionnaire answers on abortion, guns, immigration or climate found.

candidates.name: Larry Davis

summary.text: Larry Davis is a Republican candidate who describes himself as Louisiana's only America First congressional candidate. He is a lifelong Louisianan who graduated from Denham Springs High School, and his campaign emphasizes constitutional governance, limited federal spending, domestic energy and public safety.

background.text: Graduated from Denham Springs High School.
Describes himself as a lifelong Louisianan running on constitutional governance, national sovereignty and Christian conservative principles.

priorities.quote: Lowering costs for families and small businesses, reducing federal spending, securing American energy independence, and promoting workforce freedom.
Strong border enforcement, physical barriers where necessary, crackdown on cartels, mandatory employment verification, and tightening asylum loopholes.

priorities.text: Protecting parental rights and local control of education.
priorities.quote: Parents as the primary decision makers in children’s education.

statements.quote: Strong border enforcement, physical barriers where necessary, crackdown on cartels, mandatory employment verification, and tightening asylum loopholes.
statements.context: On his campaign Policies page, under "Border Security and National Sovereignty"

statements.quote: School choice and support for vocational programs.
statements.context: On his campaign Policies page, under "Protecting Parental Rights and Local Control of Education"

candidates.researchNotes: From the 12-item Policies page on his campaign site, which is written as policy summaries. No debate or questionnaire answers found.

candidates.name: Michael Mebruer

summary.text: Michael Mebruer is a Republican candidate who describes himself as a traveling medical professional and an economist with a master's degree in financial economics from LSU. He says his campaign is fully self-funded and focused on government efficiency and reducing federal debt.

background.text: Graduated from West Feliciana High School.
Earned a graduate degree from Louisiana State University in 2026; his campaign biography describes it as a master's degree in financial economics.
Works in healthcare as a traveling medical professional, with assignments that he says have taken him across the country, including Alaska.
Says his campaign is self-funded and that he is not taking donations.

priorities.text: Fiscal discipline, tax simplification, border security, protecting life and reforming major federal programs.
priorities.quote: Restoring fiscal discipline, simplifying the tax code, securing the border, protecting life, and reforming major federal programs are essential steps toward a more stable and prosperous future.

positions.summary: His campaign site says he supports legal protections for the unborn.
positions.quote: Protecting life should not only involve legal protections for the unborn

statements.quote: Michael supports mandatory nationwide implementation of the E-Verify system so that employers can quickly and reliably confirm that workers are legally authorized to work in the United States.
statements.context: On his campaign About page (written in the third person)

statements.quote: Michael supports restructuring the federal role in Medicaid to give states more flexibility while expanding access to private insurance options for low-income Americans.
statements.context: On his campaign About page (written in the third person)

candidates.researchNotes: From his campaign About page (written in the third person). No questionnaire answers found.

candidates.name: Stephen Wagley

summary.text: Stephen Wagley is a Republican candidate on the ballot for Louisiana's 6th Congressional District, with a campaign website listed by Ballotpedia. No biographical information was found.

priorities.text: Protecting the unborn, including opposing taxpayer funding of Planned Parenthood.
priorities.quote: I will fight to make sure none of our tax dollars fund Planned Parenthood.

priorities.text: Lowering prices: cutting spending and regulation and expanding domestic energy.
Securing the border and supporting President Trump's border wall.
priorities.quote: I will do everything in my power as your Congressman to support President Trump’s mission in building the wall

priorities.text: Making the Trump tax cuts permanent and simplifying the tax code.
priorities.quote: the Trump tax cuts stay permanent, the tax code is simplified

positions.summary: His campaign Issues page says life begins at conception and that he would fight attacks on Louisiana's protection of the unborn.
positions.quote: Life begins at conception. As a Christian, it is my duty to protect the unborn.

positions.summary: His campaign Issues page says he would work to block any attempt to bring back the assault weapons ban.
positions.quote: I will work to shoot down any attempt in Washington DC to bring back the assault weapons ban no matter who supports it.

positions.summary: His campaign Issues page says he supports the SAVE America Act, which he describes as requiring proof of citizenship to vote.
positions.quote: President Trump, Speaker Johnson, Majority Whip Scalise and most importantly, you my constituent, can count on my support for any and all measure to pass the SAVE AMERICA ACT.

positions.summary: His campaign Issues page says he would fight to preserve federal grants to local police and sheriffs' offices and prioritize local law enforcement in his budget submissions.
positions.quote: Our heroic police and sheriffs can count on me to fight against any effort by the Left to defund the federal grants which ensure our parish sheriffs' offices and municipal police departments to ensure they have the manpower, training, and equipment they need.

statements.quote: I will fight to secure the border and enforce the law.
statements.context: On his campaign Issues page, under "Enough Excuses. Lower Prices Now!"

statements.quote: I will fight to make sure that the Trump tax cuts stay permanent, the tax code is simplified and oppose any new federal regulations and mandates so our small businesses can succeed.
statements.context: On his campaign Issues page, under "Supporting our Businesses"

statements.quote: He has fought for school choice, veterans’ education benefits and growing the workforce to create jobs.
statements.context: On his campaign home page (written in the third person)

candidates.researchNotes: From his campaign Issues page and home page. No questionnaire or forum answers found; he was not reported at the October 2026 candidate forum covered by the Louisiana Illuminator.

candidates.name: Rufus Craig

summary.text: Rufus Craig is a self-employed attorney running as the Libertarian Party candidate. He ran for this seat in 2022, when he finished second with 13.0% of the vote.

background.text: Earned a B.S. from Louisiana State University in 1978 and a J.D. from Southern University in 1984.
Has been a self-employed attorney since 1984.
Ran as a Libertarian for Louisiana's 6th Congressional District in 2022, receiving 13.0% against incumbent Garret Graves.

candidates.researchNotes: Libertarian Party candidate page has only a short biography; no campaign website, questionnaire answers or 2026 statements on the guide's issues found (he did not respond to the Louisiana Illuminator questionnaire).

candidates.name: Chauna Banks
candidates.currentRole: Former East Baton Rouge Metro Council member, District 2 (2013–2024)

summary.text: Chauna Banks is a Democrat and former East Baton Rouge Metro Council member who represented District 2 from 2013 to 2024. She holds degrees from Southern University and ran unsuccessfully for the Louisiana House in 2023. She is running for the open 6th District seat.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in computer science and a master's degree in mental health counseling from Southern University.
Elected to the East Baton Rouge Metro Council, District 2, taking office in 2013; re-elected in 2016 over Ulysses Addison and again in 2020.
Did not seek re-election to the Metro Council in 2024; her term ended December 31, 2024 and Anthony Kenney succeeded her.
Ran for Louisiana House District 63 in 2023, advancing from the primary with 33.3% and losing the November 18 general election to incumbent Barbara Carpenter, 64.2% to 35.8%.
Qualified for the 6th Congressional District race on August 7, 2026.

record.text: Served on the East Baton Rouge Metro Council for District 2 from 2013 to 2024.

candidates.name: Patrick Forbes

summary.text: Patrick Forbes is a Democratic candidate who describes himself as an engineer and public servant with 20 years of experience in disaster recovery. He says he led the Louisiana Office of Community Development for 13 years, including recovery funding after the 2016 floods. Forbes holds two degrees from Louisiana State University.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Louisiana State University in 1984 and a graduate degree from LSU in 1995.
Describes himself as an engineer and public servant with 20 years of experience helping communities rebuild after disasters.
Says he led the Louisiana Office of Community Development for 13 years and joined Gov. John Bel Edwards in Washington to secure nearly $3 billion for recovery from the 2016 floods.

priorities.text: Lowering household bills, including backing rules against price-fixing.
priorities.quote: I’ll back real rules against price-fixing and the enforcement to make them stick.

priorities.text: Reducing home insurance costs by lowering flood and storm risk and requiring insurers to disclose the basis for rate increases.
Restoring Affordable Care Act premium help and keeping rural hospitals open.
priorities.quote: Restore the premium help that let working families buy a plan, and keep rural hospitals open and serving the communities that have nowhere else to go.

priorities.text: Restoring the Voting Rights Act and making it easier to vote.

positions.summary: Said he would reverse the cuts to Affordable Care Act subsidies and would work to repeal the Medicaid work requirements.
positions.quote: I would reverse the cuts to the Affordable Care Act subsidies,

positions.summary: His campaign site says tariffs, along with wars and tax cuts for billionaires, are driving up the cost of living for Louisiana families.
positions.quote: Reckless tariffs, misguided wars, and tax cuts for billionaires are driving up the cost of living for Louisiana families.

statements.quote: Congress is supposed to be a check on the President, not a rubber stamp, and I will lead that charge.
statements.context: On his campaign Issues page, in a section on the war with Iran

statements.quote: The current one hands the biggest breaks to the people who need them least, throws crumbs to everybody else, and has run up the largest deficits in American history.
statements.context: On his campaign Issues page, under "Rewrite the tax code"

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements from his campaign site (home page and Issues page at patforbes.com/about-pat) and a Louisiana Illuminator report. No Ballotpedia survey or other questionnaire found.

summary.text: Lindsay "Rubia" Garcia is a Louisiana educator with over two decades of experience who built a large social media following speaking about education issues. She is a Southern University Law Center graduate who interned with VOTE (Voice of the Experienced). According to her campaign biography, she is running on affordability, infrastructure, healthcare and social justice.

background.text: Born and raised in Louisiana, according to her submitted biography.

Worked as an educator for over two decades in classrooms, government programs and community organizations; served military families through the U.S. Department of Defense's Morale, Welfare, and Recreation program.
Built a social media following of over one million people speaking about education in Louisiana, according to her biography.

Organized community forums and boycotts after the 2019 Hard Rock Hotel collapse in New Orleans that killed three workers, and says she drove over 30,000 miles to support communities seeking justice for George Floyd.

Graduated from Southern University Law Center with the Justice John Paul Stevens Public Interest Fellowship; interned with VOTE (Voice of the Experienced), working to restore rights for currently and formerly incarcerated people.

priorities.text: Says she is committed to defending the Constitution, citing her legal education and work with VOTE reviewing legislation for compliance with the U.S. and Louisiana Constitutions.

Emphasizes government accountability and checks and balances, summarized in her phrase "impeach, remove, imprison, repeat," for consistent enforcement of the law against officials who violate the public trust.
Focuses on affordability and expanding economic opportunity for working families, citing her own experience with financial pressure.

positions.summary: Said she would work to bring back the Affordable Care Act subsidies, would work to repeal Medicaid work requirements, and eventually wants a taxpayer-funded national health insurance plan.
positions.quote: Healthcare is a human right in the United States,

positions.summary: In her Candidate Connection survey, says she supports raising the federal minimum wage so full-time workers are not living in poverty.

researchNotes: Surveys: Larry Davis, Michael Mebruer and Patrick Forbes completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, as did Lindsay Garcia; Blake Miguez, Rick Edmonds, Chauna Banks and Rufus Craig did not, so their biographies rely on Ballotpedia, Wikipedia and news reports. Blake Miguez and Rick Edmonds are current state senators with no accessible campaign website content stating specific issue positions. Little or no biographical information was found for Monique Appeaning and Stephen Wagley beyond their ballot status and prior candidacies.
